A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ReflecTool and the same 18-task ClinicalAgent Bench. All 20 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison; relocated content can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original CAB evaluations in Tables 2 and 5, component ablations in Table 3, and empirical sensitivity and tool-use analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds tool-selection error measurements, memory-controlled comparisons, and a tool-use case study.

M1.justification: The proposed toolbox drops ToxicityDetector and PrivacyDetector from v1 Table 4 to v2 Table 6, leaving 15 listed actions. The optimization, memory retrieval, verification procedures, Algorithm 1, and prompts remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether the removed tools participated in the reported runs.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 18 tasks across five clinical dimensions. Dataset descriptions move into Appendix B.1, but their coverage remains unchanged. The new diagnostic analyses and case study concern existing tasks rather than new datasets or test environments.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain the same LLMs, multimodal models, and COT, ReAct, CRITIC, and Reflexion baselines. New analyses reuse existing agent comparators; Table 5 varies their demonstration conditions. Inconsistent baseline citations in the new tables do not establish different comparator membership.

E3.justification: v2 adds step-level and task-level tool-selection error metrics, a comparison of fixed demonstrations versus successful trajectories from long-term memory, and an all-components-off ablation control. These extend the existing evaluation design; the benchmark splits, backbone choices, and 200-samples-per-dimension analysis subset remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's component ablations and sensitivity plots, v2 adds systematic tool-selection error analysis (Section 5.1/Table 4), memory-controlled comparisons across agents (Section 5.4/Table 5), and a retrieval-parameter failure case study (Appendix C/Figure 7). Together with the additional ablation control, these substantially expand investigation of the method's mechanisms and failure modes.

E5.justification: v1 Table 2 reports point scores without significance annotations. v2 adds markers for p-values below 0.05 and 0.01 relative to Reflexion. It does not identify the statistical test or disclose repeated-run counts, seeds, or confidence intervals, so additional runs cannot be inferred.

E6.justification: The main benchmark matrices and existing plots are unchanged, but v2 substantially expands diagnostic results. Table 4 reports step/task error values of 0.02/0.08 for candidate selection versus 1.44/4.03 for ReAct; Table 5 adds performance under two memory conditions, and Figure 7 adds contrasting retrieval outcomes. Table 3 adds the 52.37 all-off result and replaces two memory-only rows averaging 54.57 and 55.14 with a shared 54.86 row.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, Equations 1–9, and Algorithm 1 are retained. No assumptions, proofs, theorems, or derivations are added or revised; the new error measurements are empirical evaluation definitions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about CAB, the two-stage reflection framework, the two verification strategies, and performance advantages over base models and established agents. New supporting analyses do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of valid cross-dimension tool use, missing-input errors, complementary tool capabilities, and retrieval-parameter refinement in Section 5.1 and Appendices B.3/C. Section 5.4 newly attributes advantages under shared memory to tool-wise reflection, although Table 5 does not support its blanket superiority statement for both variants. The original Limitations section is unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 mainly provides tool descriptions and brief global implementation notes. v2 Appendix B.2 substantially expands reproducibility information, specifying search-result limits, retrieval implementation, tool models and APIs, SQLCoder's shared backbone and three-attempt limit, the SciSpaCy model, and document-processing software. These are newly disclosed details, not demonstrated changes to existing implementations; hardware, prompts, and the main code/data access statement remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hu et al.'s MiniCPM paper and Xie et al.'s MedTrinity-25M paper when documenting existing multimodal tools. The related-work discussion in Appendix A and the paper's principal novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The five capability descriptions move from Section 2.1 into Appendix B.1. Section 5 gains subsections, a new case-study appendix precedes the relocated experimental-details appendix, and terminology and cross-references receive limited edits. Most existing prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds two analysis tables and the case-study figure, regroups Table 3, removes the toolbox's trustfulness rows, and clarifies input icons. Table 2 gains significance markers and second-best underlining, and Figure 3's caption is corrected to optimization steps. Existing diagrams, plots, and prompt displays are retained with localized relocation and layout changes.

improvement.justification: The expanded tool implementation details and new memory controls and error analyses improve reproducibility and support for the proposed mechanism. Reporting weaknesses limit the gain: significance tests are unspecified, new tables misattribute baseline citations, and Section 5.4 overstates Table 5, where memory-assisted iterative refinement scores 59.76 below ReAct's 60.73 and Reflexion's 62.20. The evidence supports a limited net improvement rather than a substantial upgrade.
